cards.context: The lead single from The King of Limbs, released with the album on 18 February 2011. The video was nominated for Best Music Video at the 2012 Grammy Awards.
cards.headline: The video Yorke tried to bury
cards.snippet: The video — directed by Garth Jennings, choreographed by Wayne McGregor, black-and-white footage of Yorke dancing erratically, alone — nearly never came out. Yorke told Dazed in 2013: "I was deeply uncomfortable with the 'Lotus Flower' video. I did the whole thing, it was such a crack, and then they showed me the rushes the next day and I was like, 'This ain't going out.' It was like paparazzi footage of me naked or something. It was fucked up. But if it's a risk that's probably a good thing." It became one of the most-watched music videos of 2011, passed 20 million views by 2013, trended under the hashtag #thomdance, and sparked the 'Dancing Thom Yorke' meme, with people replacing the audio or editing the visuals. It now stands at about 80 million views.

cards.context: The King of Limbs was announced on Radiohead's website on 14 February 2011 and released on 18 February, a day ahead of schedule.
cards.headline: Sixteen months old before the album existed
cards.snippet: Thom Yorke debuted a solo version of "Lotus Flower" at the Echoplex in Los Angeles on 2 October 2009, while on tour with his band Atoms for Peace — sixteen months before the album appeared. On 24 January 2010, Radiohead suspended work on The King of Limbs to perform at the Music Box Theater in Hollywood, raising funds for Oxfam's response to the Haiti earthquake; at the show, Yorke performed "Lotus Flower" alone on acoustic guitar. The concert was released free online in December 2010 as Radiohead for Haiti.

cards.context: Recorded at Maida Vale Studios, London, in 2011, and released that December as The King of Limbs: Live from the Basement. This clip was uploaded to the band's channel in 2020.
cards.headline: From the Basement — the album, re-recorded live
cards.snippet: The King of Limbs was, in Nigel Godrich's words, "very mechanised" — so the band re-recorded the whole album live at Maida Vale, with Godrich producing and mixing: "a very conscious attempt… to record the album again, once it had been rehearsed and played live, to show it in a different light." Clive Deamer joined on a second drum kit. Stereogum later argued that this version of "Lotus Flower" is superior to the album's.

cards.context: Track 2 of TKOL RMX 1234567 (2011), the remix series Radiohead commissioned for The King of Limbs.
cards.headline: Jacques Greene's remix, the one that travelled
cards.snippet: Jacques Greene's 7:09 rework became the TKOL RMX project's biggest traveller: the most-watched of the series' remixes on YouTube and the most-streamed on Spotify, at 7.5 million plays. Only two remixes of "Lotus Flower" exist in the series — Greene's and SBTRKT's, which closes the album.

cards.context: The closing track of TKOL RMX 1234567 (2011). Added to the set at the owner's request, 2026-11-27.
cards.headline: SBTRKT's remix, taken on the road
cards.snippet: SBTRKT's 5:21 rework closes TKOL RMX 1234567 — and it didn't stay on the record. SBTRKT performed it live 21 times in his own sets, making someone else's remix of a Radiohead song a fixture of his own shows.
